$comment: Code-coverage exclusions under SIGNOFF.md section 4: each names the instance, the signal bits, one of the four allowed codes and the reason, and is counted only once a named person approved it. apply_exclusions.py matches these against the uncovered-items reports (measure_coverage.py --uncovered) and writes the adjusted numbers; nothing here changes what the simulator measures.

exclusions.reason: The three low column bits are the burst offset within a BL8 burst (spec memory_geometry.burst_length = 8); the address decoder issues every column aligned to the burst, so these bits are constant 0 at the controller. The queue stores them because the port width is the full column.
Same bits as X-001 seen from the scheduler: the queue entries' column and the issued command's column carry a burst-aligned column, low three bits constant under burst_length = 8.
The reset input rises once per simulation and never falls again; the init paths' assertions cover reset behaviour. A fall toggle would need a second reset, which no path applies.
